title: Check yourself: Segments, gaps and the practice: what the audit decides

questions.stem: A kind of document has exactly the minimum number of documents that the policy sets, and every one of them is correct. What does the audit decide about it?

options.text: Keep a person on it until the minimum is passed and not only met
options.says: Ruled out because reaching the minimum is enough: "A kind with exactly the minimum number is enough, and a kind exactly at the target is ready."

options.text: Automate it, with the evidence needed reached and not exceeded
Wait for the run to meet the target before looking at this kind again
options.says: Ruled out because the overall figure takes no part: "The overall figure plays no part in this decision".

options.text: Automate it only after an independent instance has rated each of the records
options.says: Ruled out because the decision rests on the two conditions and not on a further review: "A kind of document may go without a person only when two things hold".

origin.section: What a kind of document needs before a person is removed

questions.stem: The validated accuracy is 100 percent, the all-document accuracy is 95, and the policy sets a gap of five points. Does the audit call the figure overstated?

options.text: Yes, because any distance between the two figures is a warning in itself
options.says: Ruled out because small differences are normal: "A small difference is the ordinary cost of doing business."

options.text: Yes, since the validated figure is the one that matters to the customer
options.says: Ruled out because the test is a size and not a viewpoint: "The audit calls the figure overstated only when the difference is greater than a gap that the policy sets".

options.text: No, since the difference only reaches the limit and does not pass it
options.says: A difference that reaches the gap is not overstated.

options.text: No, because the all-document figure alone is a fair measure of the run
options.says: Ruled out because the two figures are reported together: "The validated figure is above the all-document figure whenever anything failed."

questions.stem: An audit finds invented values, wasted retries and unchecked totals in one run. Which fix does it name first, and why?

options.text: Add semantic checks, since they catch the largest number of defects in a run
options.says: Ruled out because a missing check comes third: "An unchecked total is a missing check, third."

options.text: Stop retrying absent values, since that wastes the most money of the three
options.says: Ruled out because a wasted retry does little harm: "A wasted retry costs money and time and corrupts nothing, so it comes second."

options.text: Let fields be null, since a wrong record that looks right travels on unseen
options.says: The order follows the damage downstream.

options.text: Measure every document, since the figures cannot be trusted until then
options.says: Ruled out because the measurement fault comes fourth: "An overstated figure is a measurement fault, fourth."
